dossier.public_summary: The dip is 25% deep and V-shaped, with odd and even dips at very different depths, implying two eclipses per orbit. The size and depth are stellar, the signal is on the target star, and individual transits vary strongly together with sector depths. Together this is an eclipsing stellar binary at twice the reported period, not a planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ by ~42% at 189 sigma, with two distinct depths (depth_ratio 1.7). This is the classic P vs 2P eclipsing binary signature, not spot variability.
Extremely V-shaped dip (best_ingress_fraction 0.4, t14_h 2.242) favours a stellar eclipse or grazing binary over a planet, despite flat-bottom being planet-like.
Diluted by zero neighbours (could_cause 0, plausible_within_1px 0) the implied companion is ~31 Rearth and ~0.5 Rstar, i.e. stellar, and centroid is on_target (offset 0.1151 arcsec).
Individual transit depths are highly inconsistent; the binary interpretation is reinforced by >2 sigma outliers.
reasons.value: p_consistent 0.0, chi2 36689.20069205744, outliers depth_ppm 318709 (55.8 sigma), 314011 (52.5 sigma)

reasons.why: Depth changes even within the same TESS-SPOC source (243402 vs 236619 ppm) - consistent with a blended/variable EB on-target, not a single planet depth.
